session_covered: US session of Friday 20 November (Europe not separately sourced)
intro: Covers the US session of Friday 20 November (Europe not separately sourced). Figures come from Trading Economics (CFD-based), Reuters via Yahoo Finance, TradingKey, Yahoo VIX, TradingView and Capital Brief; see footnotes for reconciliations.
footnotes: Index closes per TradingKey/Reuters and Trading Economics; FNArena's weekly table shows slightly different levels (S&P 6,932.65, Dow 48,225.97) that appear to be a different snapshot.
Gold: Trading Economics US$3,535 (-2.51%) used; FNArena's US$3,660 matches Thursday's level.
Gold, AUD/USD, iron ore and yield are CFD-based reference prices.

setup.summary: SPI 200 futures (Dec) are at about 8,556, down roughly 0.57% (TradingView and Capital Brief agree; Investing.com's -1.03% reflects Friday's day session only). Applied to Friday's ASX 200 close of 8,592.60 (-1.58%, a seventh straight loss and -5.4% for the week), that implies an open about 49 points (0.57%) lower, near 8,544.

local_events: No major scheduled Australian data identified today
Australian October CPI due Wednesday 25 November
Orica in focus after reported approach from Syensqo
what_moved: The AI-trade unwind accelerated: the Nasdaq fell 5.28% for its worst week since March 2020, and the S&P 500 and Dow entered correction (more than 10% below record closes), with the S&P down seven sessions in a row. Nvidia fell about 13.8% despite strong earnings amid a reported SEC probe, and AMD, Broadcom, Marvell and Applied Materials each lost more than 10%; health insurers fell on a planned Medicare Advantage audit. S&P 500 sector percentages were not available. Treasury yields fell as investors sought safety, though markets price a near-certain 25 bp Fed hike in December.

news.headline: AI selloff pushes S&P 500 and Dow into correction.
news.summary: The S&P fell for a seventh session, its longest streak since February 2020, and the VIX closed at its highest since April 2025.

news.headline: Anthropic IPO fails to steady sentiment.
news.summary: Shares closed 17.1% above the US$83 offer on Thursday, then fell 9.1% on Friday.

news.headline: Fed seen hiking in December.
news.summary: Markets price about a 99% chance of a 25 bp hike after a hot October inflation report, with Governor Waller floating 50 bp.

news.headline: Korea steps in as Kospi falls 5.2%.
news.summary: Seoul held an emergency meeting and is preparing a stock stabilisation fund.

news.headline: ASX 200 posts worst week in years.
news.summary: The index fell 1.58% Friday and 5.4% on the week after weak jobs data, following five RBA hikes this year.

news.headline: Gold falls to lowest since September 2025.
news.summary: Down 2.51% to US$3,535/oz on a hawkish Fed and stronger US dollar; copper fell 9% on the LME last week.

news.headline: Oil heads for a third weekly loss.
news.summary: Brent held near US$92.57/bbl as supply recovers and the IEA sees a surplus of about 2 million barrels per day.

coming_up: Australian October CPI, Wednesday 25 November. US markets close for Thanksgiving on Thursday 26 November.
